coverage: Nine stories · AI prompt leaks, flight outage, superconducting memory, AI shopping, game metadata, Auracast, cancer AI, emissions, Mercury

cards.headline: Planted secrets show AI prompts leaking through middleman services
cards.summary: Security researcher HD Moore sent nearly 2 million AI prompts, each hiding a unique fake password, key or link, through services that pass prompts between apps and AI models. He then watched for those "canaries" to be used. Attackers who broke into at least three AI hosting providers stole and tried the bait keys, some resellers logged prompts, and some providers ignored "don't keep my data" settings.
cards.whyItMatters: Anything you type into an AI app may travel through several companies you never chose. Never paste passwords or private information into a chatbot.

csp.connection: Data can be read at every hop where it is decrypted, so each extra system in the path adds risk.

cards.headline: Software outage delays Delta flights at the world's busiest airport
cards.summary: On Sunday, all Delta flights in and out of Atlanta were delayed after a system went down that calculates a plane's total weight and balance, including fuel, passengers and bags. Delta said staff used manual workarounds while repairing it. It followed a nationwide FAA ground stop and a multi-day Outlook outage the week before; Microsoft's president warned more outages may come as systems are upgraded.
cards.whyItMatters: Flying safely now depends on software doing math every trip. When one system fails, people need a backup plan, like doing the calculations by hand.

csp.connection: Systems need redundancy and fallback procedures so a single failure does not stop everything.

cards.headline: MIT builds a tiny superconducting memory cell that saves energy
cards.summary: Superconductors are materials that carry electricity with no resistance when very cold. MIT researchers made a thin superconducting film sandwiched between two magnetic layers; flipping the magnets turns current flow on or off, which a computer reads as a 1 or 0. The bit stays stored without power, and one cell can be changed without disturbing its neighbor. It is early lab work that still needs extreme cold.
cards.whyItMatters: Data centers use huge amounts of energy, so new kinds of memory could make future computers, including quantum ones, more efficient.

csp.connection: Any physical device with two stable states can store a bit, the smallest unit of data.

cards.headline: AI shopping helpers face a Black Friday test
cards.summary: BBC reporters asked ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Alexa to find a 55-inch TV deal. Results were mixed: several links led to dead or sold-out pages, some prices were wrong, and Alexa only searched Amazon's own store. Meanwhile, Walmart says it will let Meta's Muse AI agent shop its site for customers starting November 24, with spending limits and purchase approval.
cards.whyItMatters: AI tools can save time, but they can also be confidently wrong. Check prices and links yourself before you buy, and know who the AI works for.

csp.connection: Automated agents acting for users raise questions about accuracy, trust and control.

cards.headline: Hidden file data exposes AI music in The Binding of Isaac
cards.summary: A Reddit user found that songs in one section of the game The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus contained metadata, hidden information stored inside files, pointing to the AI music generator Suno. Steam requires developers to disclose AI use, and studio Nicalis does not appear to have done so. Creator Edmund McMillen apologized, saying he had no idea, and the files were removed within hours.
cards.whyItMatters: Files often carry more information than you can see, like where and how they were made. Players also care about whether art in games is made by people.

csp.connection: Metadata is data about data, and it can reveal a file's origin even when the content looks ordinary.

cards.headline: Off-Broadway show streams sound to headphones to share hearing loss
cards.summary: In the play Love Me, comedian Drew Michael tells stories shaped by his hearing loss. Every audience member wears headphones that receive Auracast, a Bluetooth feature that broadcasts one audio stream to any number of nearby devices. Sound designers mix clear headphone audio with muffled theater speakers so the audience experiences what Michael hears.
cards.whyItMatters: Auracast is already used for accessibility at shows, lectures and announcement systems. This play also has a feed designed for hearing aids and cochlear implants.

csp.connection: Broadcasting sends one stream to many receivers at once instead of a separate connection to each.

cards.headline: AI finds early bladder cancer clues in medical records
cards.summary: University of Plymouth researchers trained an AI model on health records from nearly 70,000 patients. It narrowed 48,261 possible factors to 38 useful ones and correctly flagged 85% of patients with bladder cancer and 91% of those without it, sometimes a year or more before diagnosis. Some links it found are correlations, not proof of cause, and more testing is needed.
cards.whyItMatters: Finding patterns across huge amounts of data could help doctors catch disease earlier and avoid unnecessary invasive tests.

csp.connection: Machine learning finds patterns in large data sets, but correlation does not show causation.

cards.headline: Meta rethinks its 2030 climate goal as AI data centers grow
cards.summary: Meta's new sustainability report says its total emissions rose nearly 40 percent, from 15.6 million to over 21.7 million metric tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent between 2024 and 2025. Meta attributed much of the increase to equipment such as data center servers. Meta says AI demand grew faster than expected and it is re-evaluating its goal of net-zero emissions by 2030.
cards.whyItMatters: Every AI request runs on physical computers that need electricity and water. Computing has real environmental costs.

csp.connection: Computing innovations can have unintended effects on the environment.

cards.headline: BepiColombo reaches Mercury orbit after eight-year trip
cards.summary: The European and Japanese BepiColombo mission is now orbiting Mercury, the planet closest to the Sun. To slow down enough, it looped past Earth, Venus and Mercury itself several times. Telemetry, data radioed back to Earth, confirmed it arrived, though a software issue made its thrusters fire for a shorter time than planned. Its two spacecraft will separate in the coming weeks.
cards.whyItMatters: Engineers control a spacecraft millions of miles away using code and data alone, so software has to be tested for problems no one can fix in person.

csp.connection: Telemetry lets engineers monitor a remote system by sending sensor data across a long-distance link.
